title: Ultrasensitive Fluorimetric Detection of Trace Se(IV) as 4,5‐Benzopiazselenol on Nonpolar Adsorbents
content:
A highly sensitive fluorimetric method for Se(IV) determination in water is proposed. It uses selective complexation with 2,3‑diaminonaphthalene and dynamic adsorption of 4,5‑benzopiazselenol onto non‑polar adsorbents (SiO2‑C8–C18, SiO2‑HPh), reaching a detection limit of 0.02 μg L−1 (SiO2‑C16). The method separates Se(VI), which can be determined by ICP‑MS.


ABSTRACT

A method for separating Se(IV) from Se(VI) has been proposed. The method is based on the formation of fluorescent 4,5-benzopiazselenol (a complex of Se(IV) with 2,3-diaminonaphthalene), which was quantitatively extracted in dynamic mode from aqueous solutions using glass preconcentrating cartridges filled with nonpolar adsorbents: SiO2-C8, SiO2-C16, SiO2-C18, and SiO2-HPh. The increase in the fluorescence intensity of the adsorbent in the preconcentrating cartridge with increasing concentration of 4,5-benzopiazselenol on its surface was used to develop a method for the solid-phase extraction (SPE)-fluorimetric determination of Se(IV) with a detection limit of 2 ng per 0.025 g of SiO2-С16 adsorbent. When using 10 mL of solution, the detection limit was 0.2 ng mL−1 (0.2 μg L−1), and when using 100 mL of solution, it was 0.02 ng mL−1 (0.02 μg L−1). The linearity of the calibration graph was maintained up to 2 μg per 0.025 g when using the SiO2-C16 adsorbent. Se(VI) did not form a complex with diaminonaphthalene and was not extracted by nonpolar adsorbents. Se(VI) passing through the preconcentrating cartridge can be determined in the effluent by ICP-MS.
